title: The first believers
hookLine: a wife, a boy, a freed slave and a best friend are the first to believe

lines: A HANDFUL OF PEOPLE IN A ROOM.
cards: Before there are crowds or history books, there's a kitchen table: a few people who say yes when saying yes looks a little crazy. Islam started like that. No announcement in the marketplace, no crowd at the Ka'ba.
Just a man telling the people closest to him what had happened in the cave, and watching their faces. Who believed first? Tradition names four people, and they're nothing alike.

teach.b: First, Khadijah, the one who wrapped him up and said Allah would never disgrace him.
Then 'Ali, his young cousin, Abu Talib's son, a boy of around ten who had been living in the Prophet's household. Then Zayd ibn Harithah.
Kidnapped as a child and sold as a slave, Zayd ended up in Khadijah's house, and she gave him to her husband.
When Zayd's father finally found him, years later, and came to buy him back, the Prophet ﷺ said: let him choose.
Zayd chose to stay. The Prophet freed him and raised him as a son.
And then Abu Bakr, his close friend, a respected merchant. Ibn Ishaq reports that the Prophet said everyone he invited hesitated at least a little, except Abu Bakr, who accepted at once.
Abu Bakr then spoke to his own friends, and Ibn Ishaq names several early Muslims, 'Uthman among them, who came in through him. Muslims don't all tell the order the same way.
One Sunni way of putting it: Khadijah first; among free men, Abu Bakr; among children, 'Ali; among freed slaves, Zayd. Shi'a Muslims emphasize 'Ali as the first male believer.
Look at them together: a wife, a child, a freed slave, a best friend, and not a single powerful man of Quraysh.
Ibn Ishaq says that for about three years the community stayed small and quiet, meeting privately, praying in secret.
The Qur'an later honors as-sabiqun, the ones who went first: those who believed before it was easy, when there was nothing to gain.

how: Muslims honor the Prophet's earliest companions and ask Allah to be pleased with them when their names are mentioned; the first believers' stories are taught to children as examples of courage and loyalty.

games.q: you're Zayd. years after you were kidnapped and sold, your father has found you and come to take you home. the Prophet says: you choose. what do you do?
games.why: Zayd chose to stay, and the Prophet freed him and raised him as a son (Ibn Ishaq).

practice: Think of something you started, a job, a move, a recovery, a family, a change in yourself, and the people who were there before it worked.
Say their names silently, one at a time, letting each face come; maybe the one who stood with you wasn't the one you expected. If you pray, you can ask Allah to reward each of them.
